reason: The uniform-in-time quantitative particle comparison requires substantially more than the existing same-marginal contraction theorem. After the declared finite ODE, coupling and sampling inputs, the solver must construct a marked-leaf representation of the time-dependent variational equation, turn the rightmost depth weight into a sum over all marked leaves, identify the exact cancellation of all zero- and one-discrepant-fat-leaf contributions, and combine the resulting quadratic decay with a noncommuting particle/nonlinear interpolation. The empirical generator identity cancels the first-order terms at total rate O(N); a genuinely second-order O(N^-2) error with integrable time decay is needed to obtain the uniform O(N^-1) term. This interaction of derivative representation, combinatorial cancellation and consistency/stability estimates supports H3, rather than the source length or propagation-of-chaos terminology.
core_assessment: The complete local proof chain is supplied. The partition attached to a marked binary tree removes singleton leaves using equal one-site marginals. The same leaf construction supplies the derivative, while the quadratic residual vanishes unless at least two leaves of size at least2 are discrepant under independent optimal leaf couplings. Its probability is quadratic in TV distance. The expected depth weight solves an exact renewal equation with decay exp(-(1-r(nu))*t). Symmetric recombination separately contracts Hamming-Wasserstein distance without any equal-marginal assumption. Finally the interpolation between the particle and nonlinear evolutions cancels its linear term through the empirical generator identity and the time-dependent variational equation, leaving only the controlled quadratic product residual.
prerequisite_assessment: Only the stated general finite-dimensional ODE/variation facts, finite Markov-generator calculus, elementary optimal coupling and product telescoping/Tonelli, and sampling collision estimate are free inputs. The local Wild representation, exact tree-weight decay, derivative contraction, quadratic remainder, Wasserstein monotonicity and actual generator cancellation were read and assessed as solution obligations. The separately referenced introductory Theorem1.5 and its canonical-data/local-CLT route are not needed for the counted empirical-error theorem.
